intro: Alabama payroll can include more than state withholding because occupational taxes may apply in some municipalities. This Alabama paycheck calculator separates the state line from an entered occupational rate so you can see what is reducing each check.

That separation also makes troubleshooting easier: if only the Alabama line differs from what you expect, focus on the state and occupational inputs rather than changing unrelated federal settings.

For married filing jointly, the $90,000 example produces $142.23 of Alabama withholding and $2,806.81 net pay, while the $130,000 example produces $209.92 of Alabama withholding and $3,975.27 net pay. sections.h3: Why your Alabama pay stub may not match the baseline examples

If your state line is unexpectedly different, compare your payroll setup with the assumptions first, then check whether an occupational deduction or other employer-plan deduction is present.
